entries.summary: At the Teutonic hospital in Bolzano, Bishop Aldrighetto of Trento invests Ulrich of Haselberg and Conrad of Greifenstein with judicial authority over Bolzano for one year. The witnesses include Friedrich, Heinrich and Reinhard von Rosenberg, explicitly described as brothers.

entries.english:
In the year of the Lord 1238, indiction eleven, on Tuesday, the third day of August, in the territory of Bolzano, at the house of the Teutonic Order’s hospital in Bolzano, in the presence of Lords Gotschalc and Caloch of Weineck, Lord Gotschalc of Avia, Lord Valschet, Lord Ulricus Wabari, Lords Fridericus, Henricus and Reinhardus, brothers of Rosenbach, Henry of Greifenstein, Symon and other witnesses.

There Lord Aldricus, bishop of the holy church of Trento, declaring it to be in the interest and for the benefit of his Casadei, invested Lords Ulricus of Haselberg and Conradus of Greifenstein with the full judicial authority of Bolzano, according to its proper extent, while reserving the rights of the gastaldus Ernestus, with every right, claim and action, as Lord Gotschalc of Weineck was formerly seen to have and hold it. From then until the next feast of Saint Genesius, and thereafter for one year and longer at the will of the lord bishop, Lords Ulricus and Conradus were to hold the judicial office of the aforesaid town of Bolzano in full, within and outside the town, giving nothing from that judicial office to the lord bishop or any of his successors. He granted them full right and power to administer justice in all matters that his other justices had formerly been accustomed to handle, to collect fines, and to perform honorably all other services legally belonging to that judicial office.

The lord bishop, for himself and his successors, promised to defend and warrant for Lords Ulricus and Conradus that gastaldate or judicial office in full, as it had been conferred on him, against every person with a lawful claim, under pledge of the property of his bishopric. He authorized them to enter into possession, and also authorized Henry of Greifenstein to place them in possession and to command all the burghers of Bolzano, each under penalty of one hundred Veronese pounds, to obey these justices and to receive and render account before them, with no contrary command or prohibition from secular authority.

This having been done, the aforesaid Lords Ulricus and Conradus, under the penalty of the fealty they had sworn to the lord bishop, promised on their pledged faith into the bishop’s hands that they would administer justice among the burghers rightly, in good faith and without fraud, and would conduct the justiceship justly to the best of their ability until the aforesaid term. I, Tridentinus, notary of the Sacred Palace, by leave and authority of the venerable father Lord Henry, by the grace of God and of the Apostolic See bishop of Trento, faithfully and lawfully drew this instrument from the abbreviated notes of the late Jacobus, notary of Bolzano, and reduced it to public form, adding or removing nothing that would change its meaning or sense; I placed my sign and subscribed.
